description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a model’s performance under external feedback, as referenced in the paper “Feedback Friction: LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback.” The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans a linear scale from 0.81 to 0.99 in increments of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 on a linear scale with major gridlines at intervals of 0.2. The blue solid line with circle markers represents “Final Accuracy,” which remains relatively high and stable across the range, starting near 1.0 at 0.81, dipping slightly to ~0.92 at 0.86, and ending near 1.0 at 0.99. The green dashed line with square markers indicates “Initial Accuracy,” which begins at ~0.55 at 0.81, fluctuates between 0.5 and 0.8, and rises sharply to ~0.95 at 0.99. The orange dashed line with diamond markers shows “Δ Accuracy” (change in accuracy), which starts at ~0.45 at 0.81, drops to a low of ~0.1 at 0.90, and ends near 0.05 at 0.99, indicating diminishing returns in accuracy gain as initial confidence increases. Error bars are present for all three lines, reflecting variability in measurements.
